correctness.rationale: For every positive integer m, the one-dimensional open-endpoint lemma gives at least 2m+1 arcs, then slicing the two-torus gives at least 4m+3 open half-squares. The explicit N=4m+3 doubled-phase covering is valid at all torus points: each first-coordinate half-arc selects 2m+1 consecutive parameters, whose second-coordinate cyclic gap pattern is 2/N repeated 2m times plus 3/N; a closed half-circle can contain at most m+1 selected starts since 2(m+1)/N>1/2. The complex angular illumination equivalence and boundary extension follow from strict inward coordinate derivatives. Exact modular finite-stratum checks for m=1..15 independently corroborate the construction; they are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Rotem–Schejter–Slomka establish ordinary (m=1) torus/bidisc coverage and fractional coverage, while Sriamorn establishes integer multiplicity for unrelated body classes and defines the natural invariant. The new statement fixes all higher multiplicities for the complex bidisc and has a separate sharp two-stage obstruction and matching explicit family. Indexed literature and accessible claim-history searches found no stated or dominating result for this complete spectrum; historical priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier torus multicover theorem or an unexamined source using equivalent cyclic-cover terminology could subsume the result.
The result does not classify optimal covering configurations; only their exact minimum number is proved.

value.rationale: This is a complete infinite multiplicity spectrum for a geometrically canonical nonsmooth four-dimensional product, extending the previously known ordinary value rather than merely producing another case. The exact law exhibits a persistent three-direction additive integer gap above the optimal fractional mass and gives an optimal cyclic construction with full endpoint control. This supports the motivated study of discrete multiple illumination and toroidal covering integrality, while making no unsupported claim for higher products.
